propositions: Pass-1 submits all chunks and agents to a 6-wide pool concurrently, causing 6 redundant cache writes of the shared system prefix when cache is cold (~3.7x token overhead versus ideal).
Warm-then-fan-out pattern already proven for container bins can reduce shared-prefix cache writes by running first call serially to warm cache, then fanning out remainder to the pool.
Gate condition requires estimated shared-prefix tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS AND >= 2 Pass-1 calls; non-systemic warm failures degrade gracefully to direct fan-out.
First single-turn chunk completes serially before pool submission begins, with subsequent calls running in parallel after cache prefix is written.
Systemic LLMUnavailableError during warm-up aborts the review; per-call cache metrics verify one write and N-1 reads of shared prefix.
